column1: Where are prompts and code context processed by the cloud-based AI assistants described in this unit?
column2: By cloud-hosted AI models.
column3: Using an assistant can send context outside your local editor.

column1: Why can a sensitive file in an open editor tab create a Copilot disclosure risk?
column2: Open-file content can become context sent to the model.
column3: Context can include more than the code at your cursor.

column1: What must you assess about database contents before enabling AI tools under a sensitive-data policy?
column2: Their data classification.
column3: Classification identifies sensitive categories such as personal or healthcare information.

column1: What compliance question must you resolve before using cloud AI with a regulated database?
column2: Whether cloud AI processing meets the applicable compliance requirements.
column3: Service safeguards do not establish your organization's approval to use the service.

column1: Why can sending a database schema to an external AI service raise intellectual-property concerns?
column2: The schema can reveal proprietary designs or trade secrets.
column3: Review organizational policies even when no table rows are sent.

column1: What determines whether GitHub Copilot in SSMS can execute a query against a table?
column2: The connected login's database permissions.
column3: Copilot access does not itself grant permission to read the table.

column1: What GitHub Copilot safeguard attempts to block harmful or insecure suggestions?
column2: Content filtering.
column3: Filters reduce risk but do not guarantee secure output.

column1: Why must AI-generated dynamic SQL receive security review even when content filtering is enabled?
column2: Filtering can still leave insecure code in suggestions.
column3: Review the code's actual handling of untrusted input.

column1: What GitHub Copilot policy can prevent suggestions that match public code from being shown?
column2: The policy that blocks suggestions matching public code.
column3: Public-code matching is distinct from detecting SQL injection.

column1: What logging mechanism gives GitHub Enterprise Cloud organizations visibility into Copilot-related activity?
column2: Audit logs.
column3: Audit logging supports oversight of tool usage.

column1: How must you prepare a password-bearing connection string before putting it in an AI prompt?
column2: Remove the password and use a placeholder.
column3: Do not send actual passwords or keys to the assistant.

column1: Why use environment variables rather than hardcoded credentials in AI-visible source files?
column2: To keep secret values out of the source files.
column3: Do not paste resolved environment-variable values into prompts.

column1: What credential-related issue must you check in AI-generated code before committing it?
column2: Accidentally included secrets.
column3: Remove real passwords or keys before code enters source control.

column1: What security principle must guide an AI-generated GRANT statement?
column2: Least privilege: grant only the permissions required.
column3: Review permission changes against the intended access model.

column1: How must untrusted data values be supplied to sp_executesql to reduce SQL injection risk?
column2: As parameters, separately from the SQL statement text.
column3: Define the parameters and bind their values instead of concatenating input into SQL.

column1: Why can AI-generated SQL remain injectable even when it calls sp_executesql?
column2: It can still concatenate untrusted input into the SQL text.
column3: The procedure name alone does not establish that the query is parameterized.

column1: What data-exposure risk must you check in AI-generated SELECT statements?
column2: Returning more data than the intended consumer is allowed to see.
column3: Apply the same review to queries inside application-facing views and procedures.

column1: What identity does the unit recommend for an MCP server's database access?
column2: A dedicated service account with least-privilege permissions.
column3: Do not give an AI database connection unnecessary privileges.

column1: What database access must a schema-only MCP task receive?
column2: Only the permissions needed to read the required schema metadata.
column3: Schema inspection does not justify broad write permissions or unrestricted row access.

column1: What network paths can an organization require instead of public-network access for sensitive MCP connections?
column2: Private endpoints or VPN connections.
column3: Choose a path that meets the organization's network-security policy.

column1: What additional disclosure risk can MCP data sampling introduce?
column2: Actual row values can be sent to the AI service.
column3: Check sampling behavior against data-handling policies before enabling it.

column1: What model-training protection does Copilot in Fabric document for your data?
column2: Your data is not used to train models.
column3: This protection does not mean that no data is sent for inference.

column1: What model-training protection does GitHub Copilot in SSMS document for your data?
column2: Your data is not used to train or retrain models.
column3: This assurance describes the documented SSMS integration.

column1: What protection secures AI-service data while it travels across the network?
column2: Encryption in transit.
column3: The unit distinguishes protection during transfer from protection in storage.

column1: What protection secures AI-service data while it is stored?
column2: Encryption at rest.
column3: Encryption does not replace organizational approval for external processing.
